rows.grounds: compound qualifying the refuge; first member sālodya, second ādi
that which has taken refuge; compound pada+āśrita

items.question: What ensures that merit grounded in sacred refuge remains imperishable?
premises: Prior acts yield enduring fruit under the stated conditions.
Taking refuge beginning with sālodya establishes a sacred basis.
What is thus grounded does not perish.
items.inference: Therefore, the merit or result associated with refuge beginning with sālodya remains imperishable.
uncertainties: The precise referent and scope of sālodyādi are not specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Therefore, O brahmin, what has taken refuge beginning with sālodya does not perish.
